flags.source_says: sigma_true = sigma_observed x sqrt[(1+phi^2)/(1-phi^2)]; at phi=0.50 multiplier sqrt(1.25/0.75)=1.291, 9% -> 11.62% (PDF p.56).
flags.derivation: GRZ filter: observed r*_t = (1-phi) r_t + phi r*_{t-1}, true returns r_t i.i.d. Then Var(r*) = (1-phi)^2 s^2 /(1-phi^2) = s^2 (1-phi)/(1+phi), so s_true/s_obs = sqrt((1+phi)/(1-phi)). Same result from the unsmoothing filter r_t = (r*_t - phi r*_{t-1})/(1-phi) with Corr(r*_t, r*_{t-1}) = phi: Var = Var(r*)(1+phi^2-2phi^2)/(1-phi)^2 = Var(r*)(1+phi)/(1-phi). Python Monte Carlo (400k draws, phi=0.5): true/observed sd = 1.730 vs sqrt(3)=1.732; the (1+phi^2)/(1-phi^2) form gives 1.291, which is wrong. 9% x 1.732 = 15.59%.
flags.evidence: PDF p.55-56, Q72 solution: 'σtrue = σobserved × √[ ( 1 + φ2 ) / ( 1 − φ2 ) ] ... At φ = 0.50 the multiplier is √(1.25/0.75) = 1.291, so a reported 9% volatility becomes 11.62%.' The same formula drives IR-FT-76 (outside this slice) whose keyed answer 11.62% would also be affected.

flags.source_says: Option (a) says the fulcrum is pushed 'lower in the structure'; the same source's solution says 'if value comes in lower, the fulcrum moves up the structure and the position is impaired' (PDF p.41).
flags.derivation: The fulcrum is where enterprise value runs out. If EV is lower, value runs out at a more senior claim, so the fulcrum migrates toward seniority (up the structure); the targeted security then falls below the fulcrum and is impaired. Moving the fulcrum 'lower' (more junior) would mean the targeted claim is better covered, not impaired, so option (a)'s clause is internally inconsistent and contradicts the solution text.
flags.evidence: PDF p.41, Q48 option (a) vs SOLUTION paragraph.
